chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masrouq Al-Nahdy, from Musa ibn Umar ibn Bazi’e, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'The people have reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he took to a road, would return via another road. So this is what he used to do.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and I do so frequently, so do it.' Then he said to me: 'Indeed, it is better for your sustenance.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of taking different roads for travel according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) validates the Prophetic tradition of varying one's route during travel, a practice rooted in seeking divine blessings and avoiding potential harm. He explicitly links this Sunnah to increased sustenance (rizq), encouraging the narrator to adopt it as a means of spiritual and material prosperity. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on emulating the Prophet’s subtle habits as a source of barakah.

en.hubeali: H 14572 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al-Haysam Bin Abu Masrouq Al-Nahdy, from Musa Bin Umar Bin Bazi’e who said:

‘I said to Al-Rezaasws that, ‘The people are reporting that the Rasool Allahsaww, whenever hesaww used to take to a road, would return via another road. So this is what hesaww used to do’. Heasws said: ‘Yes, as Iasws do so quite frequently, so do it’. Then heasws said to me: ‘But rather, it is better for your sustenance’.
en.sarwar: 124. A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al-Haysam Bin Abu Masrouq Al-Nahdy, from Musa Bin Umar Bin Bazi’e who said:

‘I said to Al-Ridha (a.s.) that, ‘The people are reporting that the Rasool Allah (saww), whenever he (saww) used to take to a road, would return via another road. So this is what he (saww) used to do’. He (a.s.) said: ‘Yes, as I (a.s.) do so quite frequently, so do it’. Then he (a.s.) said to me: ‘But rather, it is better for your sustenance’.
